2-hour cellulosic rating: Protected steel reaches ~350°C at most
 2-hour hydrocarbon rating: Protected steel stays below 538°C while external temperature hits 1100°C

This distinction has life-or-death implications. Specifying the wrong fire rating can mean the difference between structural integrity and catastrophic collapse.

## IEC Standards for International Projects [...] Hydrocarbon fires reach 1100°C within minutes. To put this in perspective:

 Standard building fires (cellulosic): 750°C maximum temperature
 Hydrocarbon pool fires: 1100°C sustained temperature
 Jet fires (pressurized release): 1200°C+ localized temperatures

At these temperatures, unprotected structural steel loses 90% of its load-bearing capacity within 10-15 minutes. This rapid deterioration is why catastrophic structural collapse happens so quickly in refinery and petrochemical fires. [...] For projects outside North America, International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standards govern fire protection requirements:

IEC 60331-11 and 60331-21: Circuit integrity standards for cables in fire conditions

 60331-11: Cellulosic fire scenarios (750°C)
 60331-21: Hydrocarbon fire scenarios (1100°C)

These standards are particularly relevant when protecting electrical infrastructure, control systems, and instrumentation in refineries and petrochemical plants.

results.content:
Propane’s autoignition temperature is 450°C (842°F), the point at which vapor in the flammable range ignites on a hot surface with no spark or flame present. That number sets the surface temperature limit for electrical equipment in classified areas, and it puts some exhaust manifolds and heating elements in range.

## Why Does Propane Vapor Collect at Floor Level? [...] Fire codes prohibit propane containers in basements, pits, or similar below-grade locations where heavier-than-air gas can collect, unless the space has approved ventilation. [...] Propane boils at -42°C (-44°F), so at any temperature you would encounter in a kitchen, a warehouse, or a Southern California parking lot, the liquid is actively boiling into vapor inside the container. NIOSH puts that vapor pressure at roughly 8.4 atmospheres at 21°C (70°F), or about 110 psi.

## Response Recommendations

What is this information?   

The Response Recommendation fields include isolation and evacuation distances, as well as recommendations for firefighting, non-fire response, protective clothing, and first aid. The information in CAMEO Chemicals comes from a variety of data sources.

Isolation and Evacuation [...] FIRE: If tank, rail tank car or highway tank is involved in a fire, ISOLATE for 1600 meters (1 mile) in all directions; also, consider initial evacuation for 1600 meters (1 mile) in all directions. In fires involving Liquefied Petroleum Gases (LPG) (UN1075), Butane (UN1011), Butylene (UN1012), Isobutylene (UN1055), Propylene (UN1077), Isobutane (UN1969), and Propane (UN1978), also refer to the "BLEVE - Safety Precautions" section.
